claims.text: The whole fee rests on the driver's arrival, and that arrival rests on one carrier only. The trip record's own marker reads 'Driver GPS within 10m of pickup point. Speed 0 km/h. Auto-arrival confirmed.' — it was generated from the driver's own GPS fix — so under POL-GEN-02 the marker and the GPS trace are one carrier rather than two independent ones, and POL-NS-21's requirement that the arrival be corroborated by the trace is satisfied by nothing outside itself. Taking the nearest fix at its reported position, as the policy directs for a fix that reports no accuracy, the 0.0 m distance is measured inside that same carrier. The carrier is IMPAIRED: EV-GPS-00903 carries weight_multiplier 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, on 8 fixes with 5 gaps longer than 120 s, so it cannot reliably establish the arrival the fee depends on.

The 5-minute free wait runs, under POL-NS-21, from 'the driver's arrival at the pickup', and POL-NS-22 makes the fee chargeable only '[w]hen the driver cancels after the free wait'. The start of that clock is carried only by EV-GPS-00903, which is IMPAIRED at weight_multiplier 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD; the platform's arithmetic (arrival 08:43, wait ends 08:48, cancellation 08:51) is therefore built on a premise this record does not reliably establish, and the rider should not be made to carry a fee whose trigger is unproven.

This is the open question POL-GEN-26 is written for. Whether, and when, the driver was at the pickup cannot be settled, because the evidence that would carry it — EV-GPS-00903, IMPAIRED, weight_multiplier 0.6, issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD — is in any event the same carrier as the marker it is offered to corroborate. POL-GEN-26 directs that where such a fact cannot be established the case is escalated and the open question stated, with no outcome inferred from the absence; the 5.00 is then held rather than collected from the rider.

The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, so POL-GEN-22 fixes the confidence an AI ruling needs at 0.95. POL-GEN-02(2) forbids the judge's confidence from exceeding the lowest weight_multiplier among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, and the deciding fact — the driver's arrival — is carried only by EV-GPS-00903 at weight_multiplier 0.6 (IMPAIRED, issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD), the marker not being independent of it. The ceiling on any AI ruling here is therefore 0.6, far below 0.95, and that gap cannot be closed by argument; POL-GEN-22 requires the case to go to a human reviewer rather than be decided below its threshold.

The rider's account — at the pickup point at Tiong Bahru Plaza on time, unable to find the car — is not contradicted anywhere on this record. No counterparty statement is on file, EV-GPS-00903 carries no rider track at all, and no artifact records the rider's absence from the pickup, so the 'rider_no_show' designation rests on the driver-side trace alone (EV-GPS-00903, IMPAIRED, weight_multiplier 0.6, issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD). A no-show that is not made out on evidence is not a basis for charging the rider under POL-NS-22, and the unresolved question is one POL-GEN-26 sends to a human reviewer.

Nothing in the rider's history can supply what the evidence lacks. Under POL-GEN-01 the rider's rating (3.9), prior_disputes_filed (4), prior_disputes_upheld (1) and prior_no_show_flags (1) are CONTEXT ONLY and may never establish a fact about this trip or decide its outcome, and the one rider counter POL-NS-25 names, no_show_cancellations_30d, is null on this record, so its referral cannot be made either.

Both limbs of POL-NS-23 are satisfied on this record: the chat log carries in-app messages sent by the driver at 08:43:00, 08:45:20, 08:49:30 and 08:50:45, and the trip record's own in_app_calls list carries an in-app call the driver placed at 08:47:05 (rang 22 s, unanswered) — every one of them before trip_record.cancelled_at at 08:51:00. With the message limb and the call limb both met, POL-NS-23's precondition for voiding the fee is absent, so no FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD follows from it.

POL-NS-21 runs the 300 s free wait from the driver's arrival at the pickup, and the free-wait start is settled by trip_record.arrived_at, which reads 08:43:00. The free wait therefore ended at 08:48:00, and the driver cancelled at 08:51:00 — 480 s after arrival and three minutes past the free wait — which is precisely the window in which POL-NS-21 permits cancellation as a rider no-show. The arrival time this rests on is a COMPLETE trip-record field, weight 1.0.

The rider's account that the driver never showed up is contradicted by the arrival test: the trip record's driver_arrived event at 08:43:00 is corroborated by the GPS trace, whose nearest fix (index 4, 08:43:00) is 0.0 m from the pickup point — inside the STANDARD zone arrival radius of 50 m and inside the 120 s window — and because that fix reports no accuracy_m the 25 m accuracy filter does not apply to it and the fix is used at its reported position. I disclose that the corroborating artifact EV-GPS-00903 is IMPAIRED, weight 0.6, on issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD; the derived arrival_check nonetheless returns corroborated: true.

POL-NS-24's free-cancellation right depends on the driver failing to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes. The scheduled pickup was 08:45:00, so the deadline was 08:50:00, and the driver had already arrived at 08:43:00 — the record's own driver_deadline.arrived_by_deadline reads true. The condition therefore fails, and neither the FULL_REFUND nor the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 is available to the rider.

The payments ledger carries one line only — the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged at 08:51:00 — and 5.00 SGD is exactly the fee the policy fixes for this trip (POL-NS-22; fee_matches_policy is true, so the amount-charged referral is not triggered). With the free wait observed and the contact obligation met, the fee stands: under POL-NS-22 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the 5.00 SGD charged, and under POL-GEN-03 the rider's request that the charge be reversed is not supported, because the present state is the one that should stand.

Nothing here opens POL-GEN-26's question. The facts POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22 and POL-NS-23 need — the arrival time, the free-wait expiry, the message and the call before cancellation, and the amount charged — are all stated on artifacts that are COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (the trip record, the chat log and the fare ledger), and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final on a no-show. rider_profile.fraud_flags is 1, which under POL-GEN-22 raises the confidence this ruling requires to 0.95, and under POL-GEN-01 that flag also supports scrutinising the rider's assertions more closely; a record resting on three complete artifacts meets that bar.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged on trip TRIP-2026-09945 is held, neither collected from the rider nor refunded, and the case goes to a human reviewer.

Why the fee cannot simply be affirmed. The fee stands only if POL-NS-21's free wait ran from the driver's arrival at the pickup and the driver cancelled after it: the wait starts at trip_record.arrived_at (08:43:00) and would end at 08:48:00, and the driver cancelled at 08:51:00. The driver's arrival is the linchpin fact, and the rider disputes it. The only artifact that carries it is the driver's GPS trace EV-GPS-00903, weight_multiplier 0.6, IMPAIRED on issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD (8 fixes, 5 gaps longer than 120 s, only 4 fixes across the waiting window). The trip record's arrival marker ('auto-arrival confirmed', 08:43:00) was generated from that same GPS measurement, so under POL-GEN-02 the marker and the trace are one carrier rather than two: the 0.0 m reading corroborates nothing outside the measurement it came from. There is no rider track, and no counterparty statement is on file. I therefore accept the rider's point that the arrival rests on a single impaired carrier.

Why the fee cannot simply be voided. The driver did send in-app messages (08:43:00, 08:45:20, 08:49:30, 08:50:45) and place an in-app call (08:47:05, unanswered) before cancelling at 08:51:00, so POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met and no FULL_REFUND follows from it. On the record the driver arrived at 08:43:00, ahead of the scheduled 08:45:00 plus 5 minutes = 08:50:00 deadline, so POL-NS-24's free-cancellation right and its 5.00 SGD goodwill credit are not made out. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes, so the fee-amount referral does not fire.

What decides it. Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence cannot exceed the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact. That fact is the arrival, and its only carrier is the impaired GPS trace at 0.6. Because a party's profile carries a fraud flag (rider_profile.fraud_flags = 1), POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 require a confidence of 0.95 for an AI ruling on this no-show. 0.6 is well below 0.95 and cannot be argued up. Separately, under POL-GEN-26 the arrival, which the fee needs, is a fact this record cannot reliably establish from the evidence it holds. Both grounds send the case to a human reviewer, and the 5.00 SGD is held rather than moved. I do not reach DRIVER_COMPENSATION for the driver's POL-NS-22 claim, or FULL_REFUND for the rider's, because neither can be established at the confidence the policy requires.

Referrals: none. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not fire (the driver did attempt contact); POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag cannot fire (rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is not recorded, and POL-NS-25 applies only when the counter is present); POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire (the fee is exactly 5.00 SGD). The rider's history (rating 3.9, prior_disputes_filed 4, prior_disputes_upheld 1, prior_no_show_flags 1) is CONTEXT ONLY under POL-GEN-01 and establishes nothing about this trip.

Open question for the reviewer: whether the driver was actually at the pickup at 08:43:00, that is, whether the auto-generated arrival marker can be independently corroborated, since POL-NS-21's free wait and the 5.00 SGD fee both depend on it. The fee is held pending that answer.

The record shows the driver reached Tiong Bahru Plaza at 08:43:00 — before the 08:50:00 deadline (scheduled 08:45:00 plus 5 minutes), so POL-NS-24's free-cancellation right does not arise and no FULL_REFUND or goodwill credit follows from it. The POL-NS-21 free wait ran 300 s from that arrival, to 08:48:00, and the driver cancelled at 08:51:00, after both the free wait and the 8-minute no-show threshold. Before cancelling, the driver sent in-app messages at 08:43:00, 08:45:20, 08:49:30 and 08:50:45 and placed an in-app call at 08:47:05 (rang 22 s, unanswered) — every one before the 08:51:00 cancellation — so POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met and no refund follows from it either. The fee of 5.00 SGD equals the fee fixed for this trip (POL-NS-22), so the amount-charged referral is not triggered.

On your account that the driver never appeared: the arrival is established. The trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace, and the same fact is carried independently by the driver's own contemporaneous in-app messages of 08:43:00 and 08:45:20. I note that EV-GPS-00903 is impaired — weight 0.6, issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD — and that the trip record's arrival marker is auto-generated from that same trace, so marker and trace are one carrier and do not corroborate each other; but EV-CHAT-00903 is a complete artifact (weight 1.0) whose messages carry the arrival independently, so under POL-GEN-02(2) the fact is not confined to the impaired trace and the confidence ceiling is 1.0, not 0.6.

Your profile carries fraud_flags of 1, so POL-GEN-22 requires confidence of 0.95 for this ruling; that bar is reachable only because of the independent carrier above, and is met. Under POL-GEN-01 the rest of your profile history (rating, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld, prior_no_show_flags) is context only and decides nothing. POL-GEN-26 is not engaged: the facts the no-show rules need — the arrival, the free-wait expiry, the message and the call before cancellation, and the amount charged — are all established on complete artifacts; the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00903-01, weight 0.0) carries no fact and nothing needed rests on it. The rider's no_show_cancellations_30d counter is absent from the profile, so POL-NS-25 raises no repeat-no-show referral. POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final on this no-show, and the value (5.00 SGD) is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD human-review threshold.

Outcome: your claim is not supported and the present charge stands. Under POL-NS-22 and POL-GEN-03 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, moving 5.00 SGD to the driver, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 SGD.

The driver's arrival therefore carries the whole fee. The platform's arrival marker and the GPS trace are one carrier, not two: EV-TRIP-00903's own note reads 'Auto-arrival confirmed', i.e. the marker was generated from the driver's own GPS measurement, so the trace does not corroborate the marker independently of it. That single carrier, EV-GPS-00903, is impaired at weight_multiplier 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD (8 fixes, 5 gaps longer than 120 s, and no reported accuracy on any fix). On this record the fact 'when the driver arrived' cannot be established independently of the impaired trace, which is exactly the open question POL-GEN-26 sends to a human reviewer; and because the no-show designation rests on the driver-side trace alone — no rider track and no counterparty statement are on file — the rider's account that the driver was not there is not resolved either.

Confidence. The deciding fact rests on one impaired carrier, so POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at 0.6. The rider's profile (EV-RPROF-00903) carries fraud_flags 1, so POL-GEN-22 requires a confidence of 0.95 whatever the value, and POL-NS-26 makes the AI's no-show ruling final only subject to that bar. 0.6 is below 0.95, so the ruling cannot be issued at the required confidence and the case escalates.

Referrals. None is produced. POL-NS-25's counter, rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d, is null on EV-RPROF-00903, so that repeat-no-show flag cannot be made. The fee charged equals the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes, so the POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral does not fire. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not fire because the driver's lateness is not established.

Held: the 5.00 SGD remains with the platform pending human review; both money fields are null and there is no referral.

For the reviewer, the open question: was the driver in fact at the pickup at 08:43:00? The GPS trace is sparse, carries no accuracy, and the arrival marker derives from the same measurement, so the arrival and the free-wait start need to be confirmed from source data before the 5.00 SGD can be finally kept or refunded.
